title: An ITM covered call is an OTM cash-secured put
summary: Selling an in-the-money call against stock that ran too far gives downside protection: you cap the upside to collect the intrinsic value plus a little extrinsic premium. At expiry this is the same payoff as selling an out-of-the-money cash-secured put at the same strike. Small differences are dividends and interest on collateral.

steps.caption: The stock ran to $100 and looks rich. We do not want to sell shares outright.
Sell the $95 call against the shares: collect $5 of intrinsic value plus a little extrinsic premium. Upside is capped.
Now sell the $95 put for cash instead. The blue line lands on top of the gold one at expiry.
The violet difference stays near zero through time. Only interest on collateral and dividends separate the two.
Both break even at the strike minus the extrinsic premium: the protection is the premium, nothing more.

takeaways: Stock + short call = short put + cash at the same strike and expiry (put-call parity).
An ITM call gives more downside cushion than an OTM call but caps upside at a lower price.
Choose the version with the better collateral, dividend and tax treatment for you.
caveats: Owning new shares conflicts with the owner's options-only rule; the deploy gate flags it.

backtest.note: Monthly 70-delta (in the money) calls sold against 100 shares, held to expiry.
